# Hugh Carrow

- **Rank:** Captain of the Freshman football team and president of the Freshman Class  <sub>[v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c6 P6](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Hugh is a tall, exceptionally good-looking youth with broad shoulders and a open-faced appearance. He has wavy chestnut hair and bright, direct, mischievous hazel/light-brown eyes. Following a winter of intense study at college, he appeared pale and thin.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P32](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0032), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 c39 P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022)_

## Personality

Hugh possesses a cheerful, mischievous nature coupled with a strong appreciation for humor. He is studious, ambitious, and highly smart with individual perspectives on life. Openly admiring and friendly, he has a resolve to extract the finest elements from existence while contributing his utmost to it. He is also selfless and generous when considering the needs of his friends.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v3 c25 P25](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0025), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036)_

## History

After returning from New Brunswick and Alberta, Hugh Carrow joined the Fourth Book class in Brierley and established a spirited academic rivalry with Nell Harcourt. Upon graduating from Regent's Academy as the Medalist, he withdrew his application for the Brierley school so Nell could remain close to Thirza, choosing instead to teach at Pale Sands to save money for college. During this time, he served as the enthusiastic president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society and contributed local notes to the Port Marlow Daily Enterprise under the pen name 'Observer'. He went on to attend Wexcombe College alongside Nell, where he was elected president of the Freshman Class, captained the Freshman football team, and led the class to victory in the Arts Rush. Though his romantic feelings were initially turned down by Nell, he remained an attentive friend, earned High Honors in Classics along with the Cooper Prize, and suffered a severe bout of typhoid fever after graduation before recovering and committing to his medical studies.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c36 P3](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0003), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c24 P0](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0000), [v2 c24 P1](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0001), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000), [v3 c6 P6](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0006), [v3 c20 P34](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0034), [v3 c39 P23](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0023), [v3 c40 P9](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0009), [v3 c40 P25](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0025), [v3 c41 P36](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0036)_

## Background by volume

- spent three years in Alberta when his father fell ill  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>
- spent a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick  <sub>[v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016)</sub>
- taught school at Pale Sands to save money for college expenses  <sub>[v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000)</sub>
- won the medal at Regent's Academy and High Honors in Classics with the Cooper Prize at Wexcombe College  <sub>[v1 c36 P3](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0003), [v3 c39 P23](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0023)</sub>

## Quotes

> I suppose Portmaris will suit us. People say it’s a pleasant old town, complete with the most splendid natural park anywhere. The landscape there is supposed to be grand, from what I’ve been told.  <sub>[v3 c1 P22](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0022)</sub>

> However, Nell, you must be prepared for a lengthy wait. Three years will pass before my studies in medicine are complete. Furthermore, even at that point, marble halls and diamond sunbursts will not be ours.  <sub>[v3 c41 P36](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0036)</sub>
